title: Product-key compute-capability frontier
question: How much factorization beam is required at higher product-key granularity to recover at least 90% of the exhaustive cosine teacher's target recall while keeping the reranking candidate fraction low?
hypothesis: Increasing factor beam should recover proposal coverage lost at higher factor granularity, producing a measurable compute-capability frontier rather than a single universally optimal setting.

endpoints.name: target_recall_retention_ratio
endpoints.definition: selective target recall divided by exhaustive cosine target recall

decision_rule.condition: For arms factor16_beam4, factor16_beam6, factor16_beam8, factor16_beam12, factor16_beam16, factor32_beam4, factor32_beam6, factor32_beam8, and factor32_beam12, report target recall, recall-retention ratio, proposal retention, states scored/M, end-to-end success, arithmetic, and routing audit values separately at each M.
decision_rule.licenses: a workload-specific compute-capability frontier for the tested product-key construction
decision_rule.does_not_license: universal optimal beam size, semantic retrieval guarantees, universal sublinear scaling, or hardware wall-clock speedup

decision_rule.condition: For each registered arm, an arm satisfies the capability constraint when target recall retention ratio is at least 0.90 at every registered M level.
decision_rule.licenses: that arm satisfies the pre-registered capability floor on the tested workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: that the arm is generally optimal or that the result transfers beyond the registered workload

held_constant: same 48 training codes versus 16 held-out target codes
same task seed stream across arms
